title: Say it while you're awake
translation: Someone once asked Hōnen: "When I sit down to chant the Buddha's name, I get sleepy and don't keep it up. How can I stop that?" He answered: "Chant it while you're awake." I think that's wonderful.
He also said: "If you think you'll be reborn in paradise, you will. If you think you might not, you might not." That's wonderful too.
And he said: "Even if you have your doubts, chant the name and you'll be reborn there." Also wonderful.
original: ある{人|ひと}{法然上人|ほふねんしやうにん}に、「{念仏|ねんぶつ}の{時|とき}{睡|ねぶ}りに{犯|をか}されて{行|ぎやう}を{怠|おこた}り{侍|はべ}る{事|こと}、{如何|いかが}して{此|こ}の{障|さは}りをやめ{侍|はべ}らむ。」と{申|まう}しければ、「{目|め}の{覚|さ}めたらむ{程|ほど}{念仏|ねんぶつ}し{給|たま}へ。」と{答|こた}へられたりける、いと{尊|たふと}かりけり。
{又|また}、「{往生|わうじやう}は、{一定|いちぢやう}と{思|おも}へば{一定|いちぢやう}、{不定|ふぢやう}と{思|おも}へば{不定|ふぢやう}なり。」といはれけり。
また、「{疑|うたが}ひながらも{念仏|ねんぶつ}すれば{往生|わうじやう}す。」ともいはれけり。
{是|これ}も{亦|また}{尊|たふと}し。
literal: When a certain person said to the holy man Hōnen, 'At the time of the nembutsu I am overcome by sleep and neglect the practice; how can I stop this obstacle?', that he answered, 'Say the nembutsu for as long as you are awake', was very holy.
Also, he said, 'Rebirth (in the Pure Land) is certain if you think it certain, and uncertain if you think it uncertain.'
Also, he said, 'Even while doubting, if you say the nembutsu, you will be reborn.'

notes.text: Hōnen (1133–1212), the founder of the Pure Land school ({浄土宗|じやうどしゆう}). He taught that anyone, monk or not, could be reborn in the paradise of the Buddha Amida just by calling on his name with faith. It was a radical simplification, and it made Hōnen very popular and very controversial.
{念仏|ねんぶつ}: here, saying the formula {南無阿弥陀仏|なむあみだぶつ} ('I take refuge in Amida Buddha'), often thousands of times a day. The translation says 'chant the Buddha's name'.
'Attacked by sleep'. {犯|をか}す: 'to violate, to overcome'. The questioner treats sleepiness as a serious obstacle ({障|さは}り) to his practice.

notes.quote: 目の覚めたらむ程念仏し給へ
notes.text: {給|たま}へ: the imperative of {給|たま}ふ, a polite 'please do'. The answer is almost too simple: chant while you are awake, and don't worry about the times you are not.
{往生|わうじやう}: 'going to be born', rebirth in Amida's Pure Land after death. In modern Japanese the word also means 'to be stuck, at a loss', and {大往生|だいわうじやう} is a peaceful death in old age.

notes.quote: 一定と思へば一定、不定と思へば不定なり
notes.text: {一定|いちぢやう}: 'certain, settled'. {不定|ふぢやう}: 'uncertain'. Faith decides it.
れ: the respectful auxiliary る, for Hōnen. けり: Kenkō reports sayings he had heard, not things he witnessed (Hōnen died long before Kenkō was born).
{尊|たふと}し: 'holy, worthy of reverence'; the translation says 'wonderful'. It comes three times, each a little shorter: いと{尊|たふと}かりけり, これも{尊|たふと}し, {是|これ}も{亦|また}{尊|たふと}し. Kenkō adds no explanation.
